newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mixed with prices trapped by fund and origin selling at the top and industry price-fixing at the lows. November ended $20 higher at $1,509 while January gave up $5 to close at $1,389. This means that the November/January spread, a barometer of nearby supply availability, ballooned again to end at $125 from Friday's close of $101 on the strength of November. Traders said funds could cover shorts if prices attempted upmoves but supply pressures, mainly from Asia and Africa, were likely to cap any substantial rally. In New York arabica futures ended higher across the board with front month December adding 50 points to close at 117.75 cents/lb. Second month March closed 60 points higher at 107.05 cents/lb. The outer months rose by 5 to 75 points. The market was nervous ahead of the release of the latest US certified stock figures but in general little or no market reaction was expected unless the stocks were to show a drastic jump. After the close, the CSCE revealed that stocks in the week to November 1 fell by 743 bags to 804 bags. This means stocks are reduced again despite the large spread, which is encouraging news for the bulls.

FUNDAMENTALS - UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks continued to decline, falling by 743 60-kg bags in the week ended November 1, to 804 bags (1,547 bags), the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said. This is the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking inventories in 1980. Stocks in New York, San Francisco and Miami remained unchanged at 61, 250 and 19 bags respectively, while stocks in New Orleans fell by 743 bags (- 36 bags) to 474 bags (1,217 bags). The fall in stocks is in line with expectations and with no stocks pending grading a week ago, traders had anticipated a further drawdown. Also this week no stocks are pending grading. This means that there could be another fall next week.

UNITED STATES - Green coffee roastings in the United States totalled about 410,000 60-kg bags during the week ended October 26, down from 460,000 bags the previous week and compared with 370,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 14.135 million bags vs 13.720 million bags in the same year-ago period.

DENMARK - Denmark imported 68,532 bags of coffee in July 1996, 1.9 percent less than in the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 to 579,600 bags, 26 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar 1995 dropped sharply by 14 percent to 873,700 bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Brazil (135,900 vs 174,600 bags) and Colombia (124,600 vs 105,600 bags). The country exported 55,300 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 16 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar 1995 dropped by 5.5 percent to 91,200 bags.
